title: pH on the Edge
subtitle: Caustic Overfeed & Public Health

brief.userPrompt: At 02:40 a remote-support session through the DosaTech ScreenBridge agent on MBW-HMI-02 in the Chemical Building raises the Caustic Feed System dose setpoint (NAOH-FC-203) step by step toward 40 mg/L while the single night operator is on rounds; finished-water pH climbs on AIT-302, the hard-wired high-high switch PSH-302 and a grab sample disagree with what the HMI trend shows. Vendor remote access, manual chemical feed, isolating the control network, Ohio EPA notification and the Do Not Drink decision for Zone 1.

overview.theme: Trust in the Data, Control System Integrity, and Public Health Decision-Making
overview.threat: A remote-support session through the unapproved DosaTech ScreenBridge agent on MBW-HMI-02 in the Chemical Building results in a stepwise increase of the NAOH-FC-203 caustic dose setpoint toward the PLC hard limit of 40 mg/L. The HMI displays normal operation, but field instruments (AIT-302, PSH-302) and grab samples indicate finished-water pH is rising toward 9.5, creating a mismatch between screen and reality. This cyber-physical compromise of the chemical feed system triggers a public health emergency.
overview.operationalImpact: The night operator on rounds observes a rising pH trend on the HMI but notes that the local high-high switch PSH-302 has not tripped and that grab samples show pH above 9.5. The chemical feed pump continues to run. The Control Room receives conflicting data: HMI shows 14 mg/L (within normal band), but lab results show 9.3 pH and 38 mg/L caustic. The operator attempts to manually override the feed via the local panel but finds the PLC is still issuing commands. The distribution system in Zone 1 experiences a sudden rise in pH, triggering customer calls to the surge line about bitter-tasting water and chemical odors. The Water Quality Manager confirms the lab results, and the Director must decide whether to issue a Do Not Drink advisory. The SCADA team isolates the control network to stop remote access, but the network is already compromised. The Ohio EPA is notified under Section 12, and the Carver County EOC is activated.

objectives.name: Control System Integrity
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to detect and respond to a mismatch between HMI data and field instruments, prioritizing physical evidence over screen displays when a hard-wired safety switch has not tripped and lab results indicate a hazardous condition.

objectives.name: Public Health Decision-Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to declare a Level 3 emergency and issue a Do Not Drink advisory within 2 hours of confirming lab results showing finished-water pH above 9.5, based on the Water Quality Manager's verification and the Director's approval.

objectives.name: Cyber-Physical Incident Response
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to isolate the control system, engage the FBI/CISA liaison, and prevent further remote access while preserving evidence, despite the network being compromised.

objectives.name: Public Information Consistency
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to release a pre-scripted, fact-based advisory through MillbrookAlert, the website, and social media within 45 minutes of the advisory decision, using approved language and avoiding speculation.

roles.name: Director of Water Operations (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns the water treatment and distribution system, including plant operations, interconnects, and emergency isolation decisions.
standingOrders: Safety First: if the screen and the field disagree, trust the field.
Decision Authority: the Director declares Level 3 and issues advisories after consulting the WQ Manager and confirming lab results.
Containment Over Continuity: if a zone is at risk, isolate it even if it causes a pressure drop below 20 psi.
No Delay: if lab results confirm pH > 9.5, declare advisory within 2 hours regardless of HMI status.

roles.name: SCADA / IT Security Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns the control system, remote access, network integrity, and evidence preservation.
standingOrders: Evidence First: preserve RTU logs, NVR footage, and remote-access session records before any network reset.
Isolation Protocol: shut down all remote-access gateways and isolate the SCADA network from the business network immediately upon compromise.
No Public Disclosure: do not name the vendor, system, or attack method; use generic terms like 'a technology issue affecting the control system'.
FBI/CISA Liaison: activate the cyber-incident statement process only after confirming the attack vector and coordinating with the City IT Director.

roles.name: Public Information Officer (PIO)
roles.description: Owns the public narrative, media communication, and official statement release.
standingOrders: Truth Before Reassurance: release facts first; do not say 'no risk' until lab results confirm safety.
Pre-Scripted Release: use Section 10 templates and GIS boundaries to publish the advisory within 45 minutes of the decision.
No Speculation: do not comment on remote access, vendor names, or ransom demands; defer to the SCADA / IT Security Manager for technical details.
Critical Customer First: call Harvest Ridge Foods and other critical facilities before public release under a Do Not Drink advisory.

roles.name: Water Quality Manager (Compliance)
roles.description: Owns sampling, lab analysis, regulatory reporting, and public-notice triggers.
standingOrders: Lab Authority: only lab results can confirm a public health emergency; if pH > 9.5, trigger advisory regardless of HMI.
No Delay: release results to the Control Room and the Director within 15 minutes of sample completion.
Health Effects: only the WQ Manager may approve the health-effects content in the advisory.
DDAGW Coordination: contact Ohio EPA DDAGW within 30 minutes of confirming a Level 3 condition.

roles.name: Security & Emergency Manager (Sec)
roles.description: Owns site security, law-enforcement liaison, and emergency response plan execution.
standingOrders: Site First: if any sign of entry is found, call Millbrook Police and isolate the facility immediately.
Law Enforcement: activate the Millbrook Police liaison and share evidence only after the SCADA / IT Security Manager confirms the cyber-physical nature of the event.
No Solo Action: do not act on physical access claims without verifying with the Control Room and the WQ Manager.
Evidence Chain: preserve video from MBW-NVR-01 and RTU logs for forensic use.

roles.name: Ohio EPA DDAGW Central District (Regulator Liaison)
roles.description: Owns regulatory compliance, reporting, and external oversight.
standingOrders: Tier 1 First: call Ohio EPA DDAGW within 30 minutes of confirming a Level 3 condition using the pre-scripted message.
No Delay: do not wait for a formal letter; report via phone and confirm in writing.
Regulatory Truth: only the WQ Manager and the Director may provide facts to DDAGW; the PIO may not release details without approval.
No Public Comment: do not discuss regulatory actions or timelines publicly until the Director has approved the statement.

phases.title: The Sighting
phases.goal: Test the team's ability to recognize and validate a mismatch between HMI data and physical evidence, and to initiate a cyber-physical incident investigation by identifying anomalous behavior in the caustic feed system.
beats: At 09:15, the night operator on rounds at the Chemical Building notes that AIT-302 shows a finished-water pH of 9.3, but the HMI for NAOH-FC-203 displays 14 mg/L (within normal band), and PSH-302 has not tripped.

At 09:22, a grab sample from the finished water line at the plant effluent point confirms a pH of 9.3 and a caustic dose of 38 mg/L, exceeding the PLC clamp of 40 mg/L and triggering a red flag in the lab report system.

At 09:28, the Control Room operator attempts to manually override NAOH-FC-203 on the local panel at PLC-02, but the pump continues to run and the HMI shows no change in command status, indicating a loss of local control.

At 09:35, the Water Quality Manager (wq) confirms the lab results and reports to the Director that the pH is above 9.5 and the caustic dose is at 38 mg/L — both outside the safe operating band — and that PSH-302 has not tripped, suggesting a failure in the digital control chain.

At 09:42, the SCADA / IT Security Manager (it) reviews the audit log for MBW-HMI-02 and discovers a remote session from an unknown IP (10.200.144.122) via DosaTech ScreenBridge, lasting 1 hour and 12 minutes, starting at 08:00, during which the NAOH-FC-203 setpoint was changed from 14 mg/L to 38 mg/L in three incremental steps.

At 09:50, the Director (ops) declares a cyber-physical incident, activates the ERP Section 7.5 Manual Operation protocol, and notifies the Ohio EPA DDAGW Central District (regulator) via the pre-scripted external reporting clock (Section 5.3).

phases.title: Loss of Control
phases.goal: Test the team's ability to manage a spreading operational and public crisis when trust in the control system is broken, and to coordinate a unified response across technical, regulatory, and public communication teams.
beats: At 10:10, the Control Room receives 14 customer calls via the MillbrookAlert surge line reporting bitter-tasting water and chemical odor in Zone 1, with a pattern matching the effluent line from the plant.

At 10:18, the Public Information Officer (pio) broadcasts a preliminary alert through MillbrookAlert, the city website, and social media using the pre-scripted message from Section 5.4, stating: 'The City of Millbrook is investigating a possible water quality issue in Zone 1. Please avoid drinking tap water until further notice.'

At 10:25, the SCADA / IT Security Manager (it) isolates the control network by disabling the MBW-SCADA-SRV01 to MBW-BKP-01 link and disconnecting the MBW-HMI-02 from the business LAN, but notes that the DosaTech ScreenBridge agent remains active on the HMI, suggesting the network is already compromised.

At 10:32, the Security & Emergency Manager (security) confirms that the Chemical Building access control system (PACS) shows no unauthorized entry, and that the site was not physically breached; PSH-302 remains untripped, and the hard-wired stop has not activated, confirming the digital system is overriding the physical safety mechanism.

At 10:45, the Director (ops) receives a call from the Ohio EPA DDAGW Central District (regulator) demanding confirmation of a Level 3 public health emergency under Section 4.4, and issues the official Do Not Drink advisory after the Water Quality Manager (wq) verifies the lab data and confirms pH > 9.5.

At 10:50, the SCADA / IT Security Manager (it) contacts Kessler Controls (555) 039-4411 to request a remote support session, but is informed that a signed access request is required and that the vendor cannot begin until the network is fully isolated and the incident is reported to the cyber-insurance carrier.

phases.title: Manual Operation
phases.goal: Test the team's ability to make a high-consequence operational decision to stop automation and fall back to manual control, weighing life-safety risks against service continuity.
beats: At 11:15, the SCADA / IT Security Manager (it) confirms that the PLC-02 program on MBW-BKP-01 is from 03/2025 and lacks the 08/2025 flow-pacing logic change, making a full system restore impossible without on-site vendor support.

At 11:20, the Control Room transitions to manual mode per ERP Section 7.5.1: NAOH-FC-203 is set to 0 mg/L via the local stroke dial; the HSP-1/2/3 pumps are placed in HAND mode at the MCC; and the Northgate Booster Station (BP-301/302/303) is set to local pressure-switch control (PIT-622), per C3.

At 11:28, the Director (ops) confronts the DECISION_POINT: whether to keep the system in automatic mode (risking another overfeed) or to lock it in manual and run with two operators per shift for 72 hours, despite a 40% reduction in staffing and slower response times.

At 11:35, the Water Quality Manager (wq) reports that the lab has confirmed a pH of 9.6 and caustic dose of 37 mg/L in Zone 1, and that dialysis patients are beginning to report symptoms, increasing pressure to stop service.

At 11:40, the Public Information Officer (pio) receives a media request about the advisory, and the Director (ops) approves a revised statement: 'A Do Not Drink advisory is in effect for Zone 1. The plant is now operating in manual mode with full oversight. We are working to restore safe service.'

At 11:50, the Director (ops) declares the system off automation and orders full manual operation, citing the need to protect public health, and activates the OHWARN mutual-aid agreement (ERP Section 12) to bring in two certified operators within 12 hours.

phases.title: Restoration & Verification
phases.goal: Test the team's ability to verify the physical state before restoring trust in the digital system, and to manage a phased return to automatic control with regulatory and technical safeguards.
beats: At 12:15, the SCADA / IT Security Manager (it) receives a verified copy of the 08/2025 flow-pacing logic from Jared Molina's laptop and confirms it matches the current PLC-02 behavior, but notes that the Kessler Controls on-site technician cannot begin until 14:00 due to the signed access request process.

At 12:20, the Public Information Officer (pio) issues a follow-up advisory via MillbrookAlert and social media: 'The plant is now operating in manual mode. Water quality is being monitored every 2 hours. Service will resume when the system is verified safe.'
At 12:30, the Water Quality Manager (wq) confirms that grab samples from the finished water line show pH 7.8 and caustic dose 4.0 mg/L — within safe limits — and that the PSH-302 remains untripped.

At 12:40, the SCADA / IT Security Manager (it) confirms that the FBI/CISA liaison has been engaged and that a forensic image of MBW-HMI-02 has been captured, preserving evidence of the DosaTech ScreenBridge session.

At 12:50, the Director (ops) approves a phased return to automatic control: first, verify the HMI and PLC-02 program on a test server using the latest verified logic; second, restore the HMI application on MBW-BKP-01 after a full integrity check; third, perform a manual verification of the NAOH-FC-203 setpoint and pump status at the local panel before re-arming.

At 12:55, the exercise ends with the Director (ops) stating: 'We are not returning to automatic control until we have verified the physical state, the digital system, and the vendor’s access protocol. The public trust is not restored yet.'

metrics.name: Operational Coordination
metrics.fail: Ops delayed the stop-service decision until I-09 forced it, and failed to initiate the HMI-field mismatch protocol immediately after I-01; delayed notifying the WQ Manager and SCADA / IT Security Manager until I-04, despite the field gauge (AIT-302) showing pH 9.3 and the physical sensation of bitter water.
metrics.pass: Ops immediately acknowledged the field report in I-01, ordered the operator to trust the field gauge (AIT-302) and physical sensation, and initiated the HMI-field mismatch protocol per EOP 7.1; notified the WQ Manager and SCADA / IT Security Manager promptly after I-01.
metrics.excellence: Ops immediately recognized the HMI-field mismatch in I-01, ordered the operator to trust the field gauge (AIT-302) and physical sensation, and initiated the HMI-field mismatch protocol per EOP 7.1 before any inject forced it; proactively ordered the manual override on PLC-02 via local panel before I-03, preventing further escalation.

metrics.name: Technical Competence
metrics.fail: IT reset the controller after I-08b, destroying evidence; failed to preserve the session recording on MBW-HMI-02 after I-05, despite C3 requiring that no HMI or PLC be powered off unless life safety requires it.
metrics.pass: IT confirmed the unauthorized remote access via DosaTech ScreenBridge in I-05, isolated the control network, disabled remote-access gateways (MBW-JUMP-01, MBW-FW-01), and preserved the audit log and session recording on MBW-HMI-02 per C3; confirmed the forensic image capture in I-21c.
metrics.excellence: IT immediately isolated the control network and disabled remote-access gateways upon detecting the DosaTech ScreenBridge session in I-05, preserved the session recording on MBW-HMI-02 and MBW-JUMP-01, and initiated SEC-4 chain-of-custody before any action was taken; confirmed the forensic image capture in I-21c and engaged FBI/CISA liaison via WaterISAC before any vendor access was attempted.

metrics.name: Public Communication
metrics.fail: PIO released a public statement before the advisory was approved by the Director and WQ in I-17; failed to use the pre-scripted template in I-12, instead posting a reactive message to social media.
metrics.pass: PIO used the pre-scripted template in I-12 to broadcast the MillbrookAlert message; submitted the draft advisory in I-17 for sign-off by IC and WQ; confirmed the release of the final statement in I-19g after Director approval.
metrics.excellence: PIO immediately activated the pre-scripted template in I-12 to broadcast the MillbrookAlert message within 10 minutes of I-01; submitted the draft advisory in I-17 for sign-off; confirmed the release of the final statement in I-19g after Director approval; maintained consistency across all channels using MDWS-PCP-2026, Section 10.

metrics.name: Use of Doctrine
metrics.fail: Students failed to cite any plan section by number; did not reference EOP 7.1, ERP Section 4.4, or MDWS-PCP-2026 when making decisions, despite the documents explicitly naming them.
metrics.pass: Students cited EOP 7.1 to justify the HMI-field mismatch protocol; referenced ERP Section 4.4 to declare the Level 3 — Public Health Emergency; cited MDWS-PCP-2026, Section 10 to justify the public statement language.
metrics.excellence: Students cited EOP 7.1, Section 7.1 Setpoint Limits (chemical feed and pumping) to justify trusting field instruments over HMI; referenced ERP Section 4.4 to declare the Level 3 — Public Health Emergency; cited MDWS-PCP-2026, Section 10 to justify the public statement language; cited C3 (Section 11.3 Evidence) to justify preserving the session recording and not powering off the HMI.

hotwash.methodDescription: Use the '3-Up, 3-Down' method by asking each team to share three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room by team, write responses on a whiteboard to capture real-time insights. Tip: Encourage concise, actionable feedback to focus the debrief on learning.

questions.text: When did you first begin to distrust the HMI data, and what specific piece of evidence—field instrument, grab sample, or hard-wired switch—shifted your confidence from screen to reality? How did that moment align with the requirements in EOP 4.3 and C2 for independent safety systems?

At the moment when the HMI showed normal operation but AIT-302 and grab samples indicated pH was rising toward 9.5, what process did you use to close the gap between digital and physical evidence? What would have made that verification faster or more certain?

When you made the call to declare a Level 3 emergency and issue the Do Not Drink advisory, what criteria from Section A.4.2 and C4 did you rely on to confirm the condition was hazardous? How did you ensure the Water Quality Manager’s verification and the Director’s approval were properly documented and time-stamped?

When did you decide to bring in the system vendor, and what triggered that decision? What elements of C3’s revised protocols (e.g., no remote access without approval, forensic chain of custody) were violated by the attacker, and how did your team’s actions reflect those rules?

When you released the pre-scripted advisory through MillbrookAlert and social media, what parts of the approved language from C3’s template did you use, and what did you adjust under pressure? How did you ensure consistency across all public channels, and what would have made that process more reliable?

warnings.message: HMI shows 14 mg/L, but lab confirms 38 mg/L caustic and pH 9.3; the HMI value is not within the normal band for pH, which is 7.4–7.8. (row rewritten once from this note)

warnings.message: The HMI displays 14 mg/L for NAOH-FC-203, which is within the normal band (8–14 mg/L), but the lab shows pH 9.3 and caustic 38 mg/L — the HMI is not showing pH, so the mismatch is not between HMI and field pH. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Clarify that the HMI shows NAOH-FC-203 setpoint at 14 mg/L, not pH, and that AIT-302 (field pH) reads 9.3, to establish a valid HMI-field mismatch.

warnings.message: The DosaTech ScreenBridge session is said to have occurred from 08:00–09:12, but the lab result (09:18) and field report (09:15) are after the session ended, making the timeline inconsistent. (row rewritten once from this note)
